title: hello-kubernetes chart values
description: Values for the hello-kubernetes Helm chart. Helm checks every install and upgrade against this schema.

global.description: Values that a parent chart shares with its subcharts. Not used by this chart.

message.description: A custom message to show on the page instead of "Hello world!". It is text, so quote it in a values file, or use --set-string, even when it is only a number.

pathPrefix.description: Serve the app under this path prefix, for example /app/hello, behind an Ingress, an HTTPRoute or your own proxy. Leading and trailing slashes are optional. Empty serves the app at /.

rewritePath.description: true: the proxy strips the prefix, and the app serves at /. The HTTPRoute does this with the standard URLRewrite filter; an Ingress needs your controller's rewrite annotation. false (recommended): the proxy passes the prefix on, and the app serves under it, with no annotations.

ingress.description: Create a networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress for the app.

enabled.description: Create an Ingress. Set service.type to ClusterIP, so the app is reached only through it.

className.description: The Ingress class, for example nginx or traefik. Empty uses the cluster's default class.

annotations.description: Annotations for the Ingress, for example your controller's rewrite annotation when rewritePath is true.

host.description: The host name for the Ingress rule. Empty matches all hosts.

tls.description: The Ingress TLS settings, as in the Ingress spec.tls field.

configured.description: Deprecated: use pathPrefix. When true, the old ingress.pathPrefix is used as the path prefix. Removed in 2.0.

pathPrefix.description: Deprecated: use the top-level pathPrefix. Used only when ingress.configured is true. Removed in 2.0.

rewritePath.description: Deprecated: use the top-level rewritePath. If either is false, the prefix is not rewritten. Removed in 2.0.

httpRoute.description: Create a Gateway API HTTPRoute (gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1) for the app. The Gateway must allow routes from the app's namespace.

enabled.description: Create an HTTPRoute. Needs at least one parentRefs entry.

parentRefs.description: The Gateways to attach to, as in the HTTPRoute spec.parentRefs field, for example [{name: my-gateway, namespace: gateway-system}].

hostnames.description: The host names for the route. Empty matches the Gateway's host names.

type.description: The Service type. LoadBalancer gives the app an external address. Use ClusterIP behind an Ingress or a Gateway, or with kubectl port-forward.

repository.description: The image repository, for example paulbouwer/hello-kubernetes or ghcr.io/paulbouwer/hello-kubernetes.

tag.description: The image tag. Empty uses the chart's appVersion. A number, such as 1.11 from --set, is used as written.

pullPolicy.description: When the kubelet pulls the image.

port.description: The port the app listens on. The probes and the Service follow it.

securityContext.description: The container securityContext, as in the Kubernetes container spec. The default meets the restricted Pod Security Standard with podSecurityContext.

podSecurityContext.description: The pod securityContext, as in the Kubernetes pod spec. The default runs the app as the numeric user 1000, which also lets older images pass runAsNonRoot.

nodeSelector.description: The node selector for the pods. The image runs on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 nodes.

resources.description: The container resource requests and limits, as in the Kubernetes container spec.

tolerations.description: The tolerations for the pods, as in the Kubernetes pod spec.

affinity.description: The affinity for the pods, as in the Kubernetes pod spec.
